title: Reconnect a car battery's positive cable
instruction: Reconnect the positive battery cable to the battery.
context: Reconnecting a battery after a replacement or a terminal clean is routine work for automotive service technicians and mechanics (SOC 49-3023: 704,640 US jobs, BLS OEWS May 2025). The stiff cable springs the clamp back up its tapered post, so one hand has to hold it fully down while the other tightens the nut; a clamp tightened high is a loose, high-resistance joint that heats and eventually leaves the car unable to start.
setup: Positions in cm on the bench, from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left; heights above the bench top. A lead-acid car battery, BCI group 24 size (26.0 x 17.3 x 22.5 cm, 18 kg, black polypropylene case), stands free on the bench, centre at x 30, y 0 (x 30.5, y -1.4 in seed 0, the screenshot's start), its long side along y and its two posts along its front edge, 2.2 cm in from the front face. The positive post (right-hand end, 8.5 cm right of the battery's centre) is an SAE lead cone 19.5 mm across at its base and 17.5 mm at its top, 18 mm tall, on a 4 mm lead boss 28 mm across, with a red mark on top and a red + on the lid behind it; the negative post (8.5 cm left of centre) is 17.9 mm at its base and 15.9 mm at its top, with a black mark and a white - on the lid. On the positive post sits the cable's clamp, held up by its stiff cable 6 mm above its seat: a lead top-post clamp, 0.14 kg with its lug, a 12-sided collar 31.1 mm across its flats and 16 mm tall with a 20.1 mm bore, two ears and an M8 pinch bolt across its front (carriage head on the right ear, a 13 mm steel hex nut, 6.5 mm thick, on the left), a crimp lug and 7 cm of red 4 AWG cable out the back, a white paint line across the nut's face (pointing up) and a white mark on the left ear beside it. A 13 mm combination wrench (chrome vanadium steel, 18.1 cm long, 0.105 kg, 12-point box end and open end) stands open end down in a tool stand centred at x 10.5, y 4 (x 11.45, y 2.8 in seed 0): a steel pedestal 6 x 7 x 12 cm with an orange-painted wooden holder on top, 5 x 4.4 x 3 cm, with a 9 mm slot along x; 2.5 kg in all. Each trial's seed moves the battery by up to 1.2 cm in x and 1.5 cm in y, tips the clamp by up to 2.5 degrees and turns it by up to 4 degrees as it is set down, and moves the stand by up to 1.5 cm in x and 2 cm in y. Both grippers start open at the ready pose.
scoring: Measured on the clamp at its outer edge, front, back, left and right: the gap to the boss (feeler gauge). Seated: every gap at most 1.0 mm, the clamp square to the post within 2 degrees and centred on it within 3 mm. Tight: the nut turned 75 to 360 degrees clockwise (seen from the nut's end) past its paint mark. Lug in line: the lug within 10 degrees of the cable's run, straight back across the battery. 1.0: seated, tight, lug in line, the wrench's box end at least 2 cm from the nut and the wrench not on or against the battery (no part of it more than 3 cm above the bench within 1 cm of the battery's outline), both grippers at least 4 cm from the clamp, the nut and the wrench, and the clamp, nut and wrench each moving less than 1 cm and 0.1 rad over the last second, held for 1 s. 0.75: seated, tight and lug in line, but the wrench still on the nut or on or against the battery, a gripper near the clamp or the wrench, or something moving. 0.5: seated and tight, lug 10 to 30 degrees out. 0.25: seated and tight with the lug over 30 degrees out; or seated with the nut turned under 75 or over 360 degrees. 0: the clamp high or crooked (once the nut has turned 20 degrees the clamp is pinched where it is; let go before that, the cable springs it back up), off the positive post or on the negative post, the battery moved more than 5 mm, or nothing done.
reset_notes: Loosen the nut back to its paint mark, set the clamp back on the post 6 mm above its seat (it stays where it is set), put the wrench back in its holder, and set the battery and the stand to the trial's marks. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Real sizes and masses (nut 30 g, real 7 g, for solver stability). The post's taper is four stacked cylinders. The collar slides on the post against 4 N of friction; the stiff cable is a spring at the lug (at most 12 N) pushing it back up until the nut, turned 20 degrees, pinches it. The nut turns past a constant 1 N m friction, not a rising torque, so tightness is its turn from the mark. The box end catches the nut by a joint when slid on square. Only 7 cm of cable is drawn.
